messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High memory and latency observed on rwd-kv-cache pool 'pool-a' starting 13:02 UTC. Memory usage > 90%, p99 latency > 800ms, error rate increase 2.7%. Trigger: continuous-batching-change-deploy-2026-03-15. Pager: pagerduty-bot triggered.
alex: ack, I'm taking pager. pulling graphs now. can someone drop the deploy id? :eyes:
priya: deploy id is cb-2026-03-15-1302, saw a diff where default_group_size went 32 -> 128. grafana shows cache items count exploded at 13:03.
cheng: looks like batch grouping created very large KV prefixes; prefix dedupe isn't kicking in because prefix TTL is unset. memory growth + background GC can't keep up.
alex: ETA 5m to test quick mitigation: disable continuous batching flag for pool-a, revert grouping to 32 if stable.
priya: i can patch feature flag via rollout API.
jo: adding quick customer impact note: several small customers reporting latency > 2s for text-gen endpoints behind this pool. no widespread 5xxs yet, but elevated tail.
alex: running command to disable continuous batching for the affected runtime:
```bash
# disable continuous batching for pool-a
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/runtime/pools/pool-a/flags" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"continuous_batching":false}'
```
alex: done. feature flag API returned 202. observing.
priya: i'm rolling back the batch group change in k8s config (helm rollback) on the rollout job.
cheng: watch cache-size metric, prefix count.
priya: helm rollback completed, new config sets max_group_size=32. restarting 2/6 pods to pick up change.
alex: noticed HPA reacting: pods scaled up from 6 -> 14 before flag flip, some OOMs in pod logs. HPA cooldown not long enough, assembly thrash.
jo: customer-facing note: posting to #support about degraded latency for small cohort, we'll update in 30m.
cheng: to reduce thrash we should bump HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds and increase scaleDown stabilization to avoid flipflop. also add a warmup prefill step.
alex: temporary HPA patch to reduce aggressive scaling while we stabilize:
```bash
kubectl patch hpa rwd-runtime-pool-a -n runtime --type=merge -p '{"spec": {"behavior": {"scaleDown": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 300}, "scaleUp": {"stabilizationWindowSeconds": 30}}}}'
```
alex: patched. scale activity reduced.
priya: restarting remaining pods to pick up both flag + config. doing rolling restart with 1 pod at a time.
cheng: adding a short-lived job to prefill top-prefixes (partial cache warmup) to avoid cold-warmup amplification:
```bash
kubectl run cache-prefill-quick --image=tools/cache-warm --restart=OnFailure -- env PREFILL_KEYS=10000 POOL=pool-a
```
jo: good. that should reduce sudden cache-miss storms.
alex: after these actions p99 latency has dropped to ~320ms, memory trending down, error rate back toward baseline. monitoring for 15m.
pagerduty-bot: Incident 82431 acknowledged by alex at 13:18 UTC.
priya: hands off to cheng for postmortem and follow-up work. I'll stay on monitoring for 15 more mins.
cheng: taking ownership. initial action items:
- root cause: continuous batching + increased max_group_size produced huge prefix groups, no TTL -> cache blowup
- mitigations done: feature flag off, config rollback to max_group_size=32, HPA stabilization increased, prefilling job run
- follow-ups: add prefix TTL/auto-eviction, add HPA synthetic-metric hysteresis, add canary for batch size change, add e2e regression test for cache growth
alex: filing incident ticket and linking logs/traces. will add timeline.
jo: support update queued: "We mitigated a performance regression; some customers experienced elevated latency. A follow-up will be sent after postmortem." :thumbsup:
cheng: assigning postmortem owner -> cheng, target: draft in 3 days. including action: evaluate default batch grouping and make safer guardrails (max group size cap, auto-ttl).
alex: thanks team. I’ll close pager once stable for 30m and confirm regen of alerts thresholds.
priya: agreed. leaving thread open for status updates.
